You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Local continual harness entries belong to this Prime Agent session. Global continual harness entries persist across Prime Agent sessions.

Use `<skill_import> ...` in shell when a CLI exists. Continual harness skill entries are Python REPL skills with an explicit Python `reference` and `arguments` contract. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

steps.output: [('ARC task-41641092: repeat motif across separator grid', 'Task-41641092 demonstrations show separator-based repetition. Identify solid separator rows/columns (colors differ from background), divide into panels, and tile/repeat the non-background motif across panels. In test grid background 6, dividers color 2 (row 4, cols 2 and 5); top-right 4x2 panel has 4 at local (2,0), 3 at (3,0). Correct output replicated these colored cells in every panel: rows 2,7 have 4 at columns 0,3,6; rows 3,8 have 3 at columns 0,3,6. Preserve divider lines/background. Demonstrations: task also supports one-dimensional copying across separator (demo 4 left panel to right) and tiling in rows/columns. Do not misread as copy entire top panel vertically; motif tiling applies per panel grid. First attempt repeating both 4/3 in all panels but was reported wrong; actual correct output differs only at assignment of 4/3 across mirrored vertical placement: correct layout has 4/3 only in leftmost column of each 2-wide panel, not rightmost. Exact output rows: [6,6,2,6,6,2,6,6], [6,6,2,6,6,2,6,6], [4,6,2,4,6,2,4,6], [3,6,2,3,6,2,3,6], divider [2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2], then same first four rows.'), ('ARC repeated pattern across separator bands task-41641092', 'Task-41641092: Identify full separator rows/columns; they divide grid into equal panels. Find the sole panel containing a non-background pattern, then copy its entire panel content (including blank/background positions) by translation into every other panel, across both row and column bands. Preserve separators. Demo: 11x5, col2 and rows3,7 separators; source is top-left 3x2 pattern [[6,6],[8,1],[1,1]], tiled into all 3x2 panels; blank rows in each panel remain blank. Test 17x11: separators row5,row11 and col3,col7; source middle-left 5x3 panel has 7 at offsets (0,2),(2,1), 9 at (1,0). Tile those positions into all nine 5x3 panels; offsets 3,4 stay background. Avoid extending pattern outside its panel or repeating anomalies in panel blank rows. Additional solved instance: test 20x19, background 3, separator color 9 at column 9 and rows 6,13; they form 2x3 panels each 6x9. Source pattern is bottom-left panel (rows14-19, cols0-8); copy its full 6x9 arrangement to all six panels, preserving separators. Demo 6x26 confirms 3 horizontal copies of source tile across vertical separators (cols8,17); tile all panels, not just same-band. Ensure output dimensions/each row width exactly match input; an earlier malformed grid submission was rejected as invalid ARC grid.'), ('ARC stripe pattern replication across separators task-41641092', 'Task-41641092: full monochromatic separator rows/columns divide grid into aligned panels/bands. Copy sparse pattern by translation to corresponding blank panels and bands, preserving separators and offset within regions. Demo 15x11: full col5 color1 splits two 5-wide panels; full row7 color1 splits two 7-high bands. Pattern in right upper panel copied to left upper, then repeated downward into lower band. Test 23x5: full col2 and rows7,15 color2. Middle band has anomalies at relative rows 0,1,3,5 on right (colors 3,6,9,8); copy to left and repeat same relative row positions in top and bottom bands. Preserve separators. Pitfall: row13 is relative index5, not 4. Earlier wrong guesses were unchanged grid and band-only replication without panel copy.'), ('ARC repeated panel motif replication', 'Task-41641092: Grid separated by full-color lines into equal panels. One panel contains sparse non-background marker pixels; copy the exact within-panel marker arrangement into all other corresponding panels, preserving separators and backgrounds. Demo: 8x26, vertical divider color4 at columns 8,17, source panel cols0-7 replicated into cols9-16 and 18-25, including all non-background colored marks. Test had separators at rows4 and cols3,7; marked panel top-middle (local offsets (0,0)=9,(1,2)=9,(2,0)=3,(3,1)=7), motif replicated across 2x3 compartments. Rule: identify the non-empty motif panel and tile its colored non-background cells across analogous panels, leaving background and divider lines unchanged.')]
